# Sandbox Proposal Context Schema

Complete field reference for the Sandbox Innovation Plan proposal context JSON.

## Top-Level Structure

```json
{
  "sandbox": {
    "basics": { ... },
    "details": { ... },
    "business": { ... },
    "plan": { ... },
    "architecture": { ... }
  }
}
```

## Section: `sandbox.basics`

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `title` | Yes | Proposal title (e.g., "AI-Powered Document Processing Platform") |
| `partner` | Yes | Partner organization name (default: "eCloudvalley") |
| `contact.name` | Yes | Primary contact person name |
| `contact.title` | Yes | Contact's job title (e.g., "Solution Architect") |
| `contact.email` | Yes | Contact's email address |
| `pdm` | Yes | Partner Development Manager name |
| `sa` | Yes | Solution Architect name |

## Section: `sandbox.details`

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `update.feature` | No | Updates for existing proposals (leave empty for initial) |
| `update.customer` | No | Target customer for update |
| `update.pain_point` | No | Customer pain point for update |
| `update.opportunity` | No | Opportunity description for update |
| `update.publish_date` | No | Update publish date, format: YYYY-MM-DD |
| `summary` | Yes | Executive summary. **Supports Markdown.** |
| `features` | Yes | Key features/capabilities. Bullet list recommended. **Supports Markdown.** |
| `solution_type` | Yes | Solution domain (e.g., "AI/ML Platform", "Data Analytics") |
| `customer_type` | Yes | Target customer segment (e.g., "Enterprise IT") |
| `pain_point` | Yes | Customer pain points. **Supports Markdown.** |

## Section: `sandbox.business`

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `justification` | Yes | Business case: market analysis, competitive advantage, expected benefits. **Supports Markdown.** |
| `aws_funding` | Yes | Requested AWS funding amount (e.g., "USD 50,000") |
| `labor_cost` | Yes | Estimated labor/delivery cost (e.g., "USD 30,000") |
| `total_cost` | Yes | Sum of aws_funding + labor_cost (e.g., "USD 80,000") |
| `start_date` | Yes | Project start date, format: YYYY-MM-DD |
| `end_date` | Yes | Project end date, format: YYYY-MM-DD |
| `release_date` | Yes | Solution release date, format: YYYY-MM-DD |
| `region` | Yes | Deployment/calculation region used by both Step 3A and Step 3B (e.g., "Asia Pacific (Taipei)"). |
| `service_list` | Yes | Step 2 authoritative service list for the AWS Calculator scenario. 3A and 3B must consume this list only in that scenario. For other scenarios, use `scripts/chrome_browser.py --print-tool-contract` and provide task/action inputs per the generic contract. |
| `service_list[*].service_name` | Yes | Canonical service display name used for verification and the proposal document (e.g., "Amazon S3"). |
| `service_list[*].search_keyword` | No | Short keyword typed into the calculator's Find Service search box (e.g., `"S3"`, `"Lambda"`, `"Step Functions"`). AWS Calculator card labels often differ from `service_name`; a concise keyword avoids search misses. Defaults to `service_name` when omitted. |
| `service_list[*].calculator_config` | No | Key/value inputs used for calculator automation form filling. |
| `service_list[*].diagram_tags` | No | Optional architecture hints used by Step 3A mapping. |
| `public_or_not` | No | Whether proposal is public: "Yes" or "No" (default: "No") |
| `case_study` | No | Allow AWS to use as case study: "Yes" or "No" (default: "Yes") |
| `calculator_link` | No | **AWS Pricing Calculator public share link** — must match `https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id=<hash>`. |
| `applied_services` | No | Service names actually added by Step 3B. Must match `service_list[*].service_name` set when present. |
| `additional_info` | No | Supplementary notes or context |

## Section: `sandbox.plan`

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `total_mandays` | Yes | Total estimated work days (e.g., "60") |
| `total_phases` | Yes | Array of delivery phases (at least 1) |

### Phase Object (`sandbox.plan.total_phases[*]`)

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `activity` | Yes | Phase name (e.g., "Planning", "Development") |
| `description` | Yes | Phase description. **Supports Markdown.** |
| `mandays` | Yes | Work days for this phase (e.g., "10") |
| `delivery_date` | Yes | Target date, format: YYYY-MM-DD |

## Section: `sandbox.architecture`

| Field | Required | Description |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| `diagram` | Recommended | Path to architecture diagram PNG (generated by `diagrams` library). Can be absolute or relative to the context JSON file. |
| `description` | Yes | Architecture description with rationale. **Supports Markdown.** |
| `applied_services` | No | Service names actually represented by the diagram. Must match `sandbox.business.service_list` set when present. |

## Validation

The `generate_proposal.py` script validates required fields and consistency gates before generating the document:

- Required field checks (same as above)
- `sandbox.business.calculator_link` regex check when provided
- `sandbox.architecture.diagram` existence check
- `service_list` parity check against `sandbox.architecture.applied_services` and `sandbox.business.applied_services` when those sets are present

Missing or invalid fields are printed to stderr with dot-notation paths (e.g., `sandbox.basics.contact.email`).

## Minimal Valid Context Example

```json
{
  "sandbox": {
    "basics": {
      "title": "My Sandbox Proposal",
      "partner": "eCloudvalley",
      "contact": { "name": "John Doe", "title": "SA", "email": "john@example.com" },
      "pdm": "Jane Smith",
      "sa": "John Doe"
    },
    "details": {
      "update": { "feature": "", "customer": "", "pain_point": "", "opportunity": "", "publish_date": "" },
      "summary": "A cloud-native solution for automated document processing.",
      "features": "- Document ingestion\n- AI-powered extraction\n- Dashboard",
      "solution_type": "AI/ML Platform",
      "customer_type": "Enterprise",
      "pain_point": "Manual document processing is slow and error-prone."
    },
    "business": {
      "justification": "Addresses growing demand for intelligent document automation.",
      "aws_funding": "USD 40,000",
      "labor_cost": "USD 25,000",
      "total_cost": "USD 65,000",
      "start_date": "2026-04-01",
      "end_date": "2026-08-31",
      "release_date": "2026-08-15",
      "region": "Asia Pacific (Taipei)",
      "service_list": [
        {
          "service_name": "Amazon S3",
          "calculator_config": {
            "storage_gb": 10,
            "put_requests": 400,
            "get_requests": 400
          },
          "diagram_tags": ["storage"]
        },
        {
          "service_name": "AWS DMS",
          "calculator_config": {
            "instance_type": "dms.t3.large",
            "instances": 1
          },
          "diagram_tags": ["migration"]
        }
      ],
      "calculator_link": "https://calculator.aws/#/estimate?id=abc123",
      "applied_services": ["Amazon S3", "AWS DMS"]
    },
    "plan": {
      "total_mandays": "45",
      "total_phases": [
        { "activity": "Planning", "description": "Requirements and design.", "mandays": "10", "delivery_date": "2026-04-30" },
        { "activity": "Build", "description": "Core development.", "mandays": "25", "delivery_date": "2026-07-15" },
        { "activity": "Release", "description": "UAT and go-live.", "mandays": "10", "delivery_date": "2026-08-31" }
      ]
    },
    "architecture": {
      "diagram": "my_architecture.png",
      "applied_services": ["Amazon S3", "AWS DMS"],
      "description": "## Overview\nUsers access via CloudFront and ALB. Backend on ECS with RDS and S3."
    }
  }
}
```
